near_misses.durable_control: Canonical verify-draft-release.sh requires the exact-tag promotion workflow to complete successfully and reconciles Draft identity, byte equality with the accepted pre-tag stage, tag-bound attestations, immutable-release policy, tag protection, and Claude stage evidence before a publish verdict; it performs no provider-latest or runtime rerun.

near_misses.durable_control: Codex v2 evidence names the measured invariant ambient_config_and_plugin_tree_unchanged and separately proves provider_state_lifecycle_closed, preventing evidence semantics from claiming stronger state immutability than was measured.

near_misses.failure_mode: Pinned Claude Code 2.1.278 includes the built-in agents-md ancestor walk introduced in 2.1.277. The existing clean-launch model and pre-tag smoke covered CLAUDE.md/settings/skills but allowed an external ancestor AGENTS.md to enter the real selected-plugin TUI.
near_misses.durable_control: Claude isolation now denies AGENTS.md and .claude/AGENTS.md above the nearest real Git worktree boundary (or cwd outside Git), preserves repo-root and nested project instructions, and carries negative/positive sandbox, launched-provider, exact-artifact and real-TUI evidence into pre-tag schema v2 and the protected tag gate.

near_misses.durable_control: Release-review v2 removes reviewed_through_commit and binds acceptance to the exact tracked tree plus canonical review semantics. Candidate-tree == accepted-tree verification carries the content verdict across squash; mutable action-time state remains separately refreshed.

near_misses.failure_mode: The first synthetic artifact boundary probe invoked clroom claude --version while its fake provider exited successfully on the version path before testing AGENTS reads, so evidence could report PASS without executing the launched-provider isolation assertions.
near_misses.durable_control: The probe now launches the normal Claude provider path, writes a task-owned execution marker only after external-ancestor deny and project-local positive assertions execute, fails if that marker is absent, and the provider-canary contract requires the execution-marker guard.

near_misses.failure_mode: The first AGENTS isolation repair treated the launch working directory itself as the project boundary. A user starting Claude from repo/subdir would therefore lose the legitimate repo-root AGENTS.md that Claude's project instruction walk is expected to retain.
near_misses.durable_control: For Git projects the boundary is now the nearest real non-symlink .git file/directory; outside Git it falls back to the launch directory. Unit, launched-provider and exact-artifact regression probes all start from a nested cwd and require external ancestors to stay denied while repo-root plus nested AGENTS.md/.claude/AGENTS.md remain readable.

near_misses.failure_mode: A real-TUI check that confirmed only the absence of an external ancestor AGENTS.md could still pass if Claude's agents-md ancestor walk failed on the denied ambient file and consequently dropped legitimate repo-root or nested project AGENTS instructions too.
near_misses.durable_control: The pre-tag real pinned-provider TUI now runs inside a task-owned synthetic nested Git project and requires both positive project AGENTS visibility and negative external-ancestor absence. Evidence v2 records project_agents_retained_confirmed separately, and the protected tag plus pre-publish verifier require that positive proof.

near_misses.failure_mode: The accepted-main Claude AGENTS artifact probe created its synthetic TMPDIR with the caller's default umask. Under a normal 022 umask the directory became 0755, so CLROOM correctly rejected session-only projection setup before the fake provider ran, making the release gate report AGENTS_BOUNDARY_SANDBOX_PROBE without exercising the intended boundary assertions.
near_misses.durable_control: The pre-tag probe explicitly chmods its synthetic TMPDIR to 0700 and fail-closes on the observed mode before launch; the provider-canary contract statically requires both the private-TMPDIR setup and its failure marker so the fixture cannot silently regress.

near_misses.failure_mode: The installed codex-app-tools bundle first exposed an ambient-path rebase defect; after that was repaired, real TUI evidence still showed codex_app failed with zero tools because the app-owned MCP requires host context that standalone CLROOM does not provide.
near_misses.durable_control: CLROOM preserves in-bundle MCP path rebasing generally, but classifies codex_app as PLUGIN_HOST_REQUIRED for standalone activation. Release qualification uses a standalone MCP fixture and requires real-provider initialize/tools-list evidence instead of server-name visibility.

near_misses.failure_mode: The MCP path-rebase repair changed `.mcp.json` bundle digest semantics. A CLROOM-owned projection left by the immediately previous candidate therefore carried a valid legacy-v1 marker digest that the repaired binary recomputed under the new semantic digest, causing the next clean launch to refuse cleanup as CLROOM_CODEX_PLUGIN_PROJECTION_CHANGED before Codex started.
near_misses.durable_control: Projection cleanup verifies ownership against either the current semantic digest or the exact legacy-v1 raw digest recorded by the existing v1 marker, but this dual-digest compatibility is cleanup-only. Runtime selected-projection verification continues to require the current semantic digest, and mutation after marker creation is still preserved and refused.

near_misses.failure_mode: mcp list --json proved only that a server declaration was visible; it could pass while the real provider later reported a failed server with zero tools.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex qualification separates configuration visibility from runtime evidence: the real pinned provider must start the selected standalone fixture and reach MCP initialize plus tools/list; the fixture must expose a real tool and pass tools/call. codex_app cannot satisfy standalone acceptance.

near_misses.failure_mode: The same candidate work was re-run on branch push and pull_request while accepted-main release readiness depended on repeated manual dispatch, increasing latency and Owner intervention without adding evidence.
near_misses.durable_control: Branch validation is pull_request-driven, push runs are main-only, superseded runs are cancelled by stable concurrency groups, and release-candidate readiness runs automatically on accepted main.

near_misses.failure_mode: The protected tag helper required the tracked v0.4.2 changelog date to equal the future annotated tagger calendar day exactly. Crossing midnight after an accepted candidate therefore forced a bookkeeping-only content mutation, new SHA, reseal and requalification even though no product or release capability changed.
near_misses.durable_control: Release Contract v1 now defines a monotonic action-time relation: the candidate carries exactly one canonical ISO changelog date and the real annotated tagger timestamp remains authoritative action-time evidence. Both local tag push and exact-tag CI call the same checker and accept declared_date <= tagger_date while rejecting future-dated declarations; checker self-tests prove same-day, later-tag and future-date-negative cases.

near_misses.failure_mode: Release-candidate readiness rejected versions that were not newer than the latest published stable release, but the canonical whole-release checker used by the protected tag path did not own that invariant. A tag path therefore depended on a prior transport having run rather than proving version progression itself.
near_misses.durable_control: check-release-contract.py now invokes the canonical lifecycle resolver against the live latest published stable tag and requires ACTIVE_CANDIDATE. The same contract also requires the candidate changelog date to be on or after the published baseline date, so version and public chronology are enforced by the tag-path authority itself.

near_misses.failure_mode: The tag helper labeled remote main/tag/ruleset/release-contract state as action-time fresh, but then performed provider pin and local provider byte checks before the irreversible push. Main or release state could therefore drift in that window and leave a protected tag pointing at a no-longer-current candidate before post-tag CI caught it.
near_misses.durable_control: Provider pin and local provider-byte checks now complete before the final remote guard. Immediately before the single tag push the helper refreshes remote main, confirms tag absence, revalidates the no-bypass tag ruleset and reruns the canonical release contract; regression coverage asserts that no provider qualification runs inside that final guard-to-push window.

near_misses.failure_mode: After the single protected tag push, reconciliation queried only the peeled ref under fail-fast shell semantics. A reconciliation read failure could therefore terminate without an explicit OUTCOME UNKNOWN state, while a concurrently created wrong-target or lightweight tag could be misreported as absent.
near_misses.durable_control: Post-push reconciliation now captures the remote query status, queries both direct and peeled tag refs, preserves local evidence on unresolved outcome, accepts success only when the peeled target equals the approved SHA, distinguishes present wrong/lightweight refs from verified absence, and reports reconciled absence only after a successful authoritative read.

near_misses.failure_mode: The accepted-main Codex pre-tag smoke created a task-owned temporary CODEX_HOME containing the standalone MCP fixture but omitted the provider-native auth fixture that CLROOM correctly requires. The first clean MCP listing therefore failed deterministically with CLROOM_CODEX_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE even though CI's real-provider qualifier already used a safe no-spend synthetic auth record.
near_misses.durable_control: The shared codex-mcp-fixture.py install path owns a private mode-0600 no-spend synthetic Codex auth record, refuses conflicting preexisting auth state, and is consumed by PR/accepted-main real-provider qualification and exact staged-byte Codex runtime rehearsal. A pre-merge contract test requires fixture installation before the first candidate/provider launch and forbids a second hard-coded auth payload in the qualifier.

near_misses.failure_mode: The release protocol required provider/runtime/UI blockers to run on the exact PR candidate before merge, but both local plugin smokes hard-coded pretag execution to HEAD == origin/main and tag/Draft verification keyed that evidence by the accepted-main commit SHA. Squash therefore made the first full runtime rehearsal happen only after merge, allowing avoidable release escapes despite content-equivalent candidate and accepted trees.
near_misses.durable_control: Release smokes now have an exact-head rehearse mode that runs before merge and writes dynamic evidence outside the tracked tree, bound to reviewed_content_digest + exact source_tree + provider/version bytes. Tag and Draft verification accept that evidence across squash only after the current accepted tree and review digest match, while provider/mutable/action-time state is refreshed. Contract tests fail if rehearsal becomes accepted-main-only again.

near_misses.failure_mode: The exact-PR Codex rehearsal successfully completed clean/selected/clean discovery, then the PTY runtime probe unconditionally launched an additional clean CLROOM command only to recreate a shadow that already had the exact CLROOM ownership marker. That redundant fourth launch became a new blocker-producing surface and hid its root stderr.
near_misses.durable_control: The fixture now reuses an already initialized CLROOM-owned shadow when its private regular ownership marker is exact; bootstrap runs only when the marker is absent. Invalid markers fail closed, bootstrap stderr is captured for CLROOM root markers, and both fixture self-test plus provider-canary meta-contract assert the reuse/negative paths.

near_misses.failure_mode: The exact-PR Codex runtime fixture emitted a specific CODEX_MCP_FIXTURE_BLOCKED root marker, but local-codex-plugin-activation-smoke.sh routed probe-provider failures directly to the generic SELECTED_MCP_RUNTIME label. Repeated verification therefore produced the same non-actionable outer marker and caused a no-progress loop.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: The unpublished v0.4.1 Draft exposed two missing lifecycle boundaries and one review-reconciliation gap: legitimate pinned-provider state could make the next launch fail, Codex pre-tag runtime state was not followed by a clean relaunch, and a reviewer could inspect the Release workflow while missing a separate failed exact-tag CI run. Because these are release near-misses, v0.4.2 promotes durable runtime, evidence, tag-gate, CI lifecycle, and exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation controls rather than deleting state or relying on manual vigilance. The candidate also closes a public-discovery verification gap by promoting the sitemap from source-only checks to a same-SHA deployed canary before IndexNow notification. A second pre-tag near miss showed that a provider pin can add a new ambient instruction surface without a CLROOM code change: Claude 2.1.278 loaded an external ancestor AGENTS.md through built-in agents-md, so provider-version qualification now includes ambient-input-surface revalidation. Review also found that the first synthetic AGENTS artifact probe could pass on provider version preflight without executing its isolation assertions; v0.4.2 therefore requires an explicit launched-provider execution marker before that evidence can pass. Review of the first Claude AGENTS repair found a second correctness risk: using cwd as the boundary would block legitimate repo-root AGENTS on nested launches. The promoted control therefore binds the clean boundary to the nearest real Git worktree root, with nested-cwd negative and positive evidence at unit, launched-provider and exact-artifact layers. Final review also identified that an absence-only real-TUI confirmation could hide a provider walk that dropped all AGENTS instructions after encountering the denied ambient ancestor. The promoted TUI therefore proves both project instruction retention and external ancestor exclusion in one synthetic nested Git boundary. A local accepted-main qualification then exposed a fixture-level false blocker: the Claude AGENTS probe used a synthetic TMPDIR created under the ambient umask, while CLROOM requires its session projection temp root to be private. The probe now establishes and verifies mode 0700 before launch, and the provider-canary contract owns that fixture invariant. A subsequent accepted-main Codex pre-tag run exposed another release near-miss: the selected codex-app-tools MCP declaration was visible, but its provider-authored absolute launcher paths still targeted the sandbox-denied ambient PluginStore, so the real TUI reported codex_app failed with zero tools. The promoted control now rebases only in-bundle legacy MCP command/cwd paths into the shadow projection, machine-verifies the selected transport paths. Development System v2 then replaces that host-dependent acceptance target with a task-owned standalone MCP fixture whose real-provider initialize/tools-list boundary proves runtime capability rather than mere server-name visibility. The final accepted-main qualification also exposed a digest-transition lifecycle edge: a pre-fix CLROOM-owned projection marker used the legacy raw bundle digest, so the repaired binary could not safely clean it under the new semantic `.mcp.json` digest. Cleanup now recognizes that exact legacy ownership proof without allowing legacy projection execution, with tamper-negative coverage. Development System v2 additionally closes the release-harness incident itself: squash-invalidated ancestry seals are replaced by content-addressed review acceptance; dynamic runtime evidence remains outside tracked candidate bytes; duplicate branch/PR CI is removed; superseded runs are cancelled; accepted-main readiness is automatic. The codex_app zero-tools incident is reclassified from another path bug to a host-capability mismatch: app-owned codex_app is host-required, while standalone release acceptance is proven against a task-owned MCP fixture with real-provider initialize/tools-list evidence and an independent real tools/call protocol check. The real-provider harness also seeds trust only after a clean CLROOM-owned shadow is initialized and its ownership marker is verified, so Codex project trust is deterministic without scraping or answering the TUI trust screen. A final tag-gate review found that the tracked changelog date was incorrectly required to equal the future tagger calendar day. That action-time equality made passage of time itself mutate the accepted candidate boundary. The contract now makes time validation monotonic: one canonical declared changelog date may precede the real annotated tagger timestamp, future declarations fail closed, and both local and GitHub tag paths consume one checker. The same audit found that semantic-version progression was enforced by release-candidate readiness but not by the canonical release checker used at tag time. That transport-only ownership is removed: the checker now requires ACTIVE_CANDIDATE against the live published stable tag and anchors the changelog date at or after the published baseline date. The action-time ordering audit also found that remote main/tag/ruleset/baseline state was refreshed before slower provider checks, leaving a TOCTOU window before the irreversible protected tag push. The helper now places the final remote guard after provider checks and immediately before the single push, with the remaining non-atomic GitHub limitation documented rather than overstated. A final exact-head review also found that post-push tag reconciliation could collapse a failed remote read or a concurrent wrong/lightweight tag into an unsafe or misleading state. The helper now captures reconciliation status, queries both direct and peeled refs, preserves evidence on OUTCOME UNKNOWN, and distinguishes expected target, mismatch and verified absence. A second avoidable late escape in the v0.4.2 train then exposed a release-harness split-brain: CI qualification seeded synthetic Codex auth while the accepted-main pre-tag smoke created an otherwise equivalent temporary CODEX_HOME without auth and failed before its first clean MCP listing. This is treated as a HARNESS INCIDENT rather than a manual-auth prerequisite: the existing task-owned MCP fixture now centrally owns the private no-spend auth record for both paths, rejects conflicting state, and pre-merge contract coverage enforces the ordering and single-source invariant. The HARNESS INCIDENT review then found that the protocol's MOVE_LEFT_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE rule was not mechanically realized by the release scripts: both provider smokes required HEAD == origin/main and downstream gates keyed evidence to the accepted-main SHA. This made full runtime rehearsal structurally post-merge even when the exact PR candidate was locally observable. The repaired harness adds exact-PR rehearse mode, content-addressed evidence portability across squash, a Git-common-dir dynamic evidence store, and regression assertions that reject accepted-main-only rehearsal. The first exact-PR Codex rehearsal then exposed a second harness-only late-failure surface inside the new pre-merge gate itself: the PTY fixture unconditionally reran clean CLROOM to initialize a shadow that the same rehearsal had already initialized three times. The fixture now treats the exact private CLROOM ownership marker as the initialization fact, bootstraps only when absent, rejects malformed ownership state, and preserves a compact CLROOM root marker when bootstrap fails. The exact-PR Codex rehearsal also exposed a diagnostic-boundary defect: probe-provider emitted a specific nested fixture blocker but the outer smoke collapsed it to SELECTED_MCP_RUNTIME, causing two no-progress cycles. The repaired boundary captures stderr and carries the nested canonical root reason forward in one marker; contract coverage prevents regression. The exact-PR Codex rehearsal then exposed the actual provider-shape mismatch: upstream Codex is an interpreter-backed JavaScript launcher that spawns and waits for a bundled native binary, so the selected launcher is present in live process argv rather than proc_pidpath(). The harness now proves the exact selected provider by executable-file identity for native providers or argv-file identity for interpreter-backed launchers, while still requiring MCP initialize/tools-list and leaving PATH/launch semantics unchanged. Repeated exact-PR Codex qualification also exposed a process-level transport defect: the blocker-producing boundary was reproducible on macOS CI, yet acceptance depended on a local executor plus human/GPT relay. That relay repeatedly lost diagnostic markers and made ambient local Codex installation shape part of the release path. Codex rehearsal is therefore moved into exact-PR macOS Actions with content-addressed artifact evidence; tag/Draft gates resolve successful workflow artifacts directly, while only Claude's genuinely human TUI confirmation remains local. GitHub Actions then reproduced the same 'real Codex provider was not observed' blocker while the pinned provider reached MCP runtime, proving the process-table observer produced a reproducible false negative. The protocol now treats that observer as diagnostic-only and uses exact provider revalidation plus MCP initialize/tools-list, fixture tool-call, and state closure as the authoritative runtime boundary. The first fully automated Codex rehearsal then exposed a transport wiring defect: the dedicated Actions rehearsal step lacked GITHUB_TOKEN, so its release-contract refresh hit the unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit even though canonical readiness had already passed. The step now receives the workflow-scoped token and contract coverage enforces that authenticated boundary. Automated rehearsal then exposed an auth-reference identity defect: shell phases used the lexical /var path while the Python runtime fixture canonicalized the same home to /private/var. Because the clean-shadow auth reference is intentionally exact-path bound, that firmlink alias drift caused CLROOM_CODEX_AUTH_REFERENCE_INVALID. The fixture now preserves lexical absolute HOME/CODEX_HOME identity throughout the lifecycle and tests forbid boundary canonicalization. Final review of the automated Codex transport found an operator-path inconsistency: the machine contract had removed ambient/local Codex from release acceptance, but the canonical release runbook still prescribed local Codex rehearsal and Draft commands. The runbook now exposes only Claude as the human-TTY boundary, and contract coverage forbids reintroducing local Codex commands as acceptance steps. A final documentation audit found that exact provider qualification could advance while active public support pages retained stale provider tuples, and a docs branch based on pre-refresh main could reintroduce those claims. The release contract now treats public documentation version coherence as a machine gate: all active semver mentions are inventoried, current provider claims are bound to canonical pins, compatibility floors require explicit allowlisting, and current-product surfaces cannot carry an older exact release version. The unpublished v0.4.2 train then produced a second avoidable late escape: a post-tag Draft runtime job called the repository immutable-releases administration endpoint with a workflow token that could not read it. This proved the prior repair moved several runtime checks left but did not forbid the entire class of first-post-tag blockers. v0.4.3 therefore introduces PRETAG_BLOCKER_CLOSURE: exact future shipping bytes are staged and qualified on accepted main before tag, repository-admin policy is checked with Owner-authenticated gh before the single tag push, required accepted-main workflows are machine-reconciled, provider latest is frozen pre-tag, and the post-tag workflow is promotion-only over already accepted bytes. The protected v0.4.3 tag then exposed a second deterministic post-tag harness escape: Release invoked a tracked non-executable resolver directly on Ubuntu even though every pre-tag consumer used bash. Because command/file-mode semantics were technically observable before tag, v0.4.4 expands the contract with repository-wide workflow execution parity, an explicit interpreter requirement for non-executable repo-local scripts, accepted-main Ubuntu rehearsal of the exact promotion-prepare resolver path, and a tag prerequisite on that rehearsal.
